Note shape Length · Attack · Decay · Sustain

Note envelope

ShortOverlapping

Length follows the note rate; above 100% lets notes overlap. Attack rises to full level, decay settles to sustain, then the note fades out. Long attack and decay times fit inside short notes.

Off · notes begin at their own pitch

Subtle bendFull interval

Slides from the previous note toward the next. At 100%, the slide starts at the previous pitch; lower amounts make a smaller bend. Time fits before the note fades out. The first note starts cleanly.

Repeats current-chord tones into higher octaves to fill the pool. This voice has its own range, separate from the canvas. It follows tempo and rhythm speed, with the voices’ reverb and delay.

PLACE THE SOUND 01
BRIGHT · LIGHTLOW / LEFTHIGH / RIGHTWARM · LONG

Left to right chooses pitch and stereo position. Up high is lighter and brighter; down low is fuller, warmer, and longer.

SIX WAYS TO PLAY 02
01

Touch

Place a single note. Depth shapes its weight, tone, length, and color bloom.

02

Draw silk

Move slowly for soft, lingering notes and smooth ribbons of fluid.

03

Rush & flick

Fast strokes make bright, short accents and forceful jets. A flick releases a final spark.

04

Orbit

Draw circles to make whirlpools, widen stereo motion, and open the whole scene’s tone.

05

Gather & bloom

Hold still until a ring grows, then release a small cloud of long chord tones.

06

Conduct

Sweep up to open the composition’s filter, or down to warm and soften it. It settles after release.

Let it rainA little serendipity on autopilot
No right notes. Just your notes.
WELCOME TO CHROMAFLOW

A small space to play.

Click the canvas to release a droplet. It falls, blooms into the fluid, and plays a note from the current chord.

Choose a color to use only that color and voice for painting, automatic rain, and blooms. Turn on Cycle colors beside the palette for random colors and voices: all four are used before repeating, with no consecutive repeats. The horizontal position moves from low notes to high notes, always within your chord. In Perform → Place the sound, choose how many octaves below and above the base chord the canvas spans. The Perform tab includes Quantize: switch it on and choose a note length to line up splashes and notes with the beat. It also explains how height, speed, circles, and holds shape the fluid and sound. Slow strokes linger; fast strokes accent. Hold still, then release to bloom. Sweep vertically to conduct the whole scene.

The canvas follows the harmony with colored light, slow currents, and a gentle bloom as each chord arrives. Adjust Chord atmosphere in the Fluid tab to set its strength.

Press Begin listening to enable sound. With Let it rain on, droplets arrive on their own. Turn it off for a completely hands-on instrument.

The Sound tab includes an optional arpeggiator. Choose one instrument, a pattern, 1–16 chord tones, and a note rate. Open Note shape to control length, attack, decay, and sustain. It follows the current chord automatically and traces its notes across the scene.

Open the Rhythm tab to add optional percussion. The beat studio has four voices and sixteen editable steps. Hits can send ripples across the scene, stir the existing fluid, or both.
